summary: Arizona Game & Fish regulates 'restricted live wildlife' by family — and the rat family (Muridae) is NOT on the restricted list, so a roof rat needs no special license to keep, breed, or rehome. Importing non-restricted mammals is also allowed without a Game & Fish license. The one requirement is a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection to bring the animal in from out of state (Dept of Agriculture), plus the universal no-release rule. (Legal basis is 'unrestricted wildlife,' since Arizona's narrow definition of 'domestic' doesn't fit a species that still exists in the wild — but the practical result is the same: no permit needed.)

keep.why: R. rattus (family Muridae) is not among the rodent families designated 'restricted live wildlife' in A.A.C. R12-4-406, and a special license is required only to possess restricted wildlife. With no listing, no Game & Fish license is required to keep one.
keep.governing_law: A.A.C. R12-4-406 (restricted list — Muridae absent); R12-4-402; R12-4-401.

breed.why: Game & Fish special-license/breeder rules attach to restricted wildlife; private game-farm/propagation licenses cover game birds, not murid rodents. Because R. rattus is unrestricted, breeding privately held animals needs no Game & Fish license.

sell_give.why: Prohibited activities (sell/give/trade absent a license) apply to restricted wildlife under R12-4-402(A); they don't reach a non-listed species, so transferring/adopting out roof rats isn't barred. A high-volume commercial dealer should confirm with Game & Fish whether any dealer license is triggered.

transport.why: Intrastate transport of an unrestricted species isn't licensed; R12-4-405 allows importing non-restricted mammals without a Game & Fish license. But the Dept of Agriculture (A.A.C. R3-2-602) requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection for animals imported into Arizona (the rule's 'animal' includes rodents), so carry a CVI on import. Never release (R12-4-402(A)).
transport.governing_law: A.A.C. R12-4-405; A.A.C. R3-2-602 (import CVI); R12-4-402(A) (no-release).

restrictions.summary: Bringing a pet rat into Arizona requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (A.A.C. R3-2-602); no Game & Fish import license is needed for an unrestricted species.
restrictions.where_to_file: Arizona Dept of Agriculture, State Veterinarian

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat into the wild — prohibited under A.A.C. R12-4-402(A) and ecologically harmful.
